title: Capacity SLO Canary Framework + Autoscale Financial Guardrails (Q3)
creator: Lina Chen
description: Develop a repeatable canary framework that validates Capacity SLOs for Dedicated pools and enforces financial guardrails for autoscale operations. This ticket scopes the product and operations requirements to: 1) define measurable SLOs for dedicated pool availability and tail latency under autoscale events, 2) create automated canary runs that exercise warm-pool -> scale-up -> drain workflows, and 3) implement budget/threshold-based guardrails and alerting to prevent runaway autoscale spend during rollouts or demand spikes.
goals: Define end-to-end Capacity SLOs (P95 cold-start latency, P99 tail, error-rate) for dedicated pools
Ship an automated canary harness that runs on every autoscale policy change and major runtime release
Introduce financial guardrail signals (burst burn rate, projected 24h spend) with automatic soft-stop and human-in-loop escalation
Reduce dedicated-pool incident surface related to scale events by 40% in Q3
metrics: SLO-1: P95 response latency for short gen (<=512 tokens) < 120ms during steady-state
SLO-2: P99 tail latency < 400ms when autoscale adds new instances
SLO-3: Error rate for scale events < 0.5%
Financial guardrail: projected 24h autoscale spend growth rate capped at 15% over baseline without manual approval
Canary pass rate >= 98% across the defined workload matrix before rollout
canary_plan: Create workload matrix: small/medium/large batch mixes + short/long seq distributions
Add canary pipeline in CI that triggers on runtime- and autoscale-policy PRs
Run canaries against staging dedicated pools with synthetic traffic and real KV cache patterns
Collect telemetry: latency distribution, queue length, instance spin-up time, error traces
Automatic judgement: if canary violates SLOs or increases projected spend beyond guardrail, abort rollout and create incident ticket
financial_guardrails: Implement 'soft budget' for each pool: daily cap and 24h rolling projected spend signal
Alert levels: inform (10% above baseline), throttle suggestions (15%), hard soft-stop (20%) requiring on-call approval
Expose projected spend delta in Console rollout UI and in canary run outputs
Add billing simulation mode for canaries to estimate cost impact of new autoscale settings before production deploy
acceptance_criteria: Confluence PR describing SLO definitions and canary matrix reviewed and approved by Eng and SRE
CI canary pipeline created and green for a runtime PR (example runtime-1.22 canary run)
Console shows projected spend delta for a sample autoscale policy and surfaces guardrail warnings
Playbook for manual escalation documented and linked from rollout UI
risks: Synthetic canaries may not fully emulate customer KV-cache warmup patterns leading to false positives/negatives
Aggressive financial guardrails could delay legitimate emergency scale-ups and impact customer experience
Telemetry gaps around instance spin-up timing may make automated judgement flaky
Cross-team coordination (SRE, runtime, finance, console) is required and could slow delivery
next_steps: Schedule kickoff with runtime and SRE (target week 2025-07-14)
Draft SLO definitions doc and circulate for review by 2025-07-11
Prototype canary job in CI using small staging pool by 2025-07-25
Design Console copy and visual for projected spend by 2025-08-01
